newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa condemns Sierra Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa condemns Sierra Leone coup.

text.p: South Africa said on Monday it was extremely concerned about an army coup in Sierra Leone and called for the leaders to give up their attempt to seize power.
On Sunday Sierra Leonean soldiers of the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council ousted the civilian government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and installed military rule in the West African country.

"The South African government is extremely concerned...this is a major setback to a process of democratisation in Sierra Leone to which the international community attached great importance," a foreign ministry statement said.
Pretoria called on the army to abandon the coup.
"The South African government hopes that the democratically elected government of Sierra Leone will be restored to power without delay," the statement added.

South Africa has cultivated a high-profile approach to African diplomacy recently as both President Nelson Mandela and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki tried to halt the civil war in Zaire, now renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo.

But a foreign ministry spokesman said the country had no plans to mediate in Sierra Leone, where Major Johnny Paul Koromah has appointed himself the new head of state, unless it is asked to get involved by local parties.
"We didn't initiate contact in Zaire either. We have had no such request from Sierra Leone. Let's see what happens if we get it," the spokesman said.

The coup comes on the eve of next week's Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Zimabwe. Pretoria said the Sierra Leonean army's actions were a setback to a democratisation process on the continent which the OAU meeting had hoped to foster.
"It constitutes a flagrant disregard of this encouraging trend," the statement said.
